div.div: 2 بغّضهُ ٱللّٰهُ إِلَى النَّاسِ , (S, TA,) or لِلنَّاسِ, (Msb,) [but this I think doubtful, from what is said in explanation of the verb of wonder, (see 4,)] inf. n. تَبْغِيضٌ, (S, K,) God rendered him hateful, odious, or an object of hatred, to men; (S, Msb; *) تَبْغِيضٌ being the contr. of تَحْبِيبٌ: (K:) or very hateful or odious. (TA.) You say also, حُبِّبَ إِلَىَّ زَيْدٌ وَ بُغِّضَ إِلَىَّ عَمْرٌو [Zeyd was rendered an object of love to me, and 'Amr was rendered an object of hatred, or of much hatred, to me]. (A, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
